a.text: I was fifteen when I entered the Witch King's Spire.
I came from an ordinary family in Kreis Einwald. I should not have been able to become a noble's attendant, but I heard that Herkunftshorn made no distinction between nobles and commoners.
This was not because he treated commoners particularly well, but because he looked down equally on all who cowered at the foot of his throne.
At first, my job was to clean his instruments. But Herkunftshorn no longer played ordinary music, and those instruments had no meaning.
Later, I was sent to clean the resonance pipelines at the top of the Spire. It was not a difficult job, but Herkunftshorn would not tolerate even a single speck of dust in them.
My colleagues came and went. Few got to leave on their own two feet. In the end, I was the only one left, quietly cleaning at the top of the tower.
And a thousand sunrises and sunsets later, the Witch King's Spire fell.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Cut off the way down.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Attention all squads. Find the Sankta. Do not allow her to enter the amphitheater and interrupt the performance of the Güldenesgesatz.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: The target is known to use unusual Arts. You have permission to kill if necessary.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hello. Were you looking for me?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: —Barrier up!

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Get in formation! Catch her!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Arturia Giallo.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Leithanien took you in when you became a pariah in Laterano. Countless nobles honored you for your remarkable musical talent.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: The Kaiserinnen granted you rights equivalent to spire nobility.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: So return to your cell and submit to them, and they may yet allow you to live.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That was never an option.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What point is there to living if I can't play freely?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Then accept your death.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Your Arts have gotten stronger.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: You missed your chance to break out, Sankta.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: The Güldenesgesatz is in progress. Do you see the scene outside? Your parlor tricks are meaningless before the golden glory of Leithanien.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yes, I can feel that your will is firmer than ever.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But is it your will expressing that music, or has the melody convinced you that what you see is what you think?

spans.text: will expressing that music, or has the melody convinced you that what you see is what you think?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: That's irrelevant. The golden melody guides me. My will echoes along with it!

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: You, our enemy, will melt before Leithanien's radiance—

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: ...She's gone?

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: An illusion? But there was no music!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Why does everyone keep assuming that I create illusions?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I warned you. When your emotions are being controlled by a melody that doesn't belong to yourself, you can easily overlook the reality before you... Like where I moved to in that 'radiance.'

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Behind—

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Barrier— too late—

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Now, I would like to ask you to kindly remove the Arts cast on my instrument.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: There, it's clean now. Danke.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: How did we... lose to you?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Normally I wouldn't stand a chance, but your souls have become stiff and inflexible due to the bindings of the Güldenesgesatz, creating innumerable weaknesses in your Arts.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: But... why? With Arts like these, you could have changed your destiny, enjoyed wealth, fame, and favor beyond reckoning... What meaning is there in defying the Kaiserinnen?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hm, I think we have very different views on the meaning of meaning.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fame, fortune, status... All merely accessories to a soul that will eventually wither and rot with the passage of time.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Kurfürst, beggar, or myself, the only difference is in the whispers of our hearts.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I want to climb the tallest spire. Because of a melody, a soul, and a future.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And for a promise I made to a friend.

a.text: Ten years had passed since the death of the Witch King. I was attending the funeral of an old friend.
After the funeral, I saw a Sankta with her cello in the amphitheater below the Twin Spires. Others came and went, but she stood there from noon until sundown.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: According to legend, even the clouds stopped for the Witch King when he played up on his spire.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I wonder... do the clouds remember what the Spire looked like back then?

a.text: I suppose not. Clouds change so quickly, after all.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: My teacher often told me of how he stood beneath the Witch King's Spire while it was still standing, playing for the sole sovereign of Leithanien.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The golden-red clouds embraced the dark spire like an extravagant robe.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: He wanted to come back and see the spectacle again, but wasn't allowed to participate in Das Kaiserinnensfest. In fact, he could barely get permission to leave his home.

a.text: Herr Emmanuel was one of the Witch King's musicians, after all, even if just for a short while. Times were hard for him after the Witch King's demise.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Few came to say their goodbyes, and you were the only one to truly shed tears for him.

a.text: I heard your playing at the funeral. It was very touching.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Danke.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But that doesn't bring even the slightly bit of comfort to my teacher.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I asked to play for him while he was still alive, but he refused. During his days of pain and hardship, he refused to dwell on the happiness of the past, nor did he seek any change.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: He simply shut himself in his room, playing the Güldenesgesatz over and over again.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Through that unchanging melody, he drowned himself in Leithanien's greatness. Forgetting love, forgetting hate, and forgetting himself.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yet, when faced with death, his heart was still filled with... regret.

a.text: I've heard far too much regret over these long years.
My image of Herr Emmanuel remained that of the energetic old man who thanked you with a hearty laugh when you passed him his instrument.
I heard that, in the end, he was too weak to even lift a bow.
I thought that without the shadow of the Witch King's Spire, the skies of Leithanien would change greatly.
I thought that, going from Vedunien to Zwillingstürme, from the Witch King's Spire to the Twin Empresses' Spires, the melody echoing in the dusk would be somehow different.
But both then and now, we are like the clouds, unable to control where we drift.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Why are you not going downstairs?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I have no interest in this sort of 'concert.'

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A melody that binds the listener's will is just another form of law.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: How did you know—

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As complex as your Arts are, their structure is clearly visible to those familiar with Originium Arts and music. In that sense, it's different from Laterano's law.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Music should come from the unrestrained breathing of the soul, but you turned it into a cornerstone of order, all to control people's wills and wear down their emotions.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: True bonds between souls are growing weaker. People are increasingly unable to understand one another, unable to respect the emotions of one another, and as such do harm to one another.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Such a rigid melody is no music at all.

steps.name: Imperial Caster
steps.text: Ugh—!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We're almost at the top. I should start preparing for the next piece, before this one ends.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's almost time to make good on our promise, isn't it?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: As you said, this is a good place to play... or listen.

a.text: Is this my deepest memory?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yes.

a.text: Sorry.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Why apologize?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Very few have invited me to play their heart's music of their own accord. Most did whatever they could to escape. Yet you have bared your soul to me... For that, I am grateful, and overjoyed.

a.text: I just thought I could show you the death of the Witch King through my memories.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: My music simply follows the melody of your heart. It cannot decide what you recall. All I can do is feel your emotions, and recreate them.

a.text: Sounds like sculpting, then.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You could say that. I discover and record, rather than changing one's true visage.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: There is only one reason we cannot enter the Witch King's Spire in your memories.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Whenever you recall his death, there is a... hand that truly moves your emotions.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A hand that grabbed you amidst that great flood of Arts.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Whose hand was it?

a.text: Whose hand was it?
It was...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Look out!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: They're coming one after another. Federico and I will try to hold them off.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You're blind, and it's too risky. Grab my hand and stay close.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: ...You're so much like him.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You mean... my father?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: This is just like when he grabbed me under the Witch King's Spire... He grabbed the hand of a servant he'd never met, and protected me through one wave of Arts after another.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...You were in the Spire the night the Witch King died.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You never told me that was how you met.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Ja.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I had just lost my sight, and was cowering before the half-collapsed stairs. Neither the Witch King's guards nor the Twins' soldiers would have paid any heed to a humble servant.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Instead, a squad from Sturmland found me.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It was led by Werner, looking for his missing father and brother in the Spire.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: His heart must have been fraught with worry, but he couldn't ignore me shivering in a corner, and pulled me out of the ruins himself.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...That sounds like him alright.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I would have done the same.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You're both good people. Very good people.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It's such a shame that...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why are you covering my ears?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: No need to be afraid, Viviana.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It'll pass. This will all pass.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What's happening?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The music has changed.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's... It's hideous!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: My head... who's attacking me?! It's like someone stuffed a thousand screaming fowlbeasts into my brain!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: These fireworks, too! The colors! It's so crass!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: This is wrong. This isn't right. Am I playing it wrong? Is everyone wrong?

spans.text: This is wrong. This isn't right. Am I playing it wrong? Is

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Herr from Sturmland? Are you alright?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: D-Don't touch me! I don't know who you are, and I don't want to know! Are you the one who played it wrong? Are you trying to break something? Everything?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Ugh—euuggh!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Something went wrong with the melody?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But how could everyone be wrong at the same time?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And how could a simple mistake lead to something so... painful?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Look at the Twin Empresses' Spires.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's him. Herkunftshorn. I'd recognize that anywhere. His power is eating away at the Güldenesgesatz!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The Witch King's remnants... where are they?! I knew there were some left. It's time to fight, Lessing!

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: ...You're not affected?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: By a few dark clouds? After what I've had to live with in my head every day of my life?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...The Güldenesgesatz itself, though.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It made me miss Urtica. Now that is deeply disturbing.

spans.text: It made me miss Urtica. Now

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: That's the power of the Movement.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: It defines Leithanien and its beliefs.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't want someone else deciding what I should miss, what I should love, and what I should praise.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But I'm guessing that whoever it is that's sabotaging the performance is after more than just pranking the Kaiserinnen and the nobles outside Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Enemy on your left.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I know. Your side, too.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Let's do this together.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: I didn't think anyone would retain their senses.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: For once, I'm grateful for everything you've done to me. Pain and chaos in my brain are like old friends by now.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: ...Good work.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You too.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So why are you acting just fine while everyone else is in agony? I'm beginning to suspect that you're a Lich-sculpted wooden puppet.

spans.text: acting just fine while everyone else is in agony? I'm beginning to suspect that you're a Lich-sculpted wooden puppet.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I was trained from a very young age to deal with this kind of situation.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And what kind of situation would that be?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The collapse of the Güldenesgesatz.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Please tell me you're joking.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Do you see the golden glow rising over the edge of the amphitheater?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I've never seen so many Gesatzswächter in one place at the same time.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Her Majesty's order—

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Surround Gnade Avenue and Macht Avenue.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Do not allow the corrupted Güldenesgesatz to spread.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So many Gesatzswächter... and Gendarmerie.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The entire Zwillingstürmeshof will be on lockdown before long.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Haha, it's no use! It's too late.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Herkunftshorn is back! The one true king has returned to a Leithanien that rightfully belongs to him!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Quiet, please.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: We're leaving.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Viviana...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Cora, please, promise me... Don't say or do anything for now.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I might have tried something if it were just Herr Reiner, but there are too many of them, and each one the equal of a Knight-Champion.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Why do you not speak? Why should we hide now that the curtain is about to rise?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Our dream, our obsession, the moment for which we have given both blood and soul is finally upon us!

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: So why is there no joy on your face?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Concertm—

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I told you to be quiet.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You knew.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Since when?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I visited Marigold Alley before I went to see Arturia.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I wanted to see those drawings again, the images that gave me such warmth.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But I didn't find anything.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: All the drawings, the ones with marigolds in them, the ones with clues leading to the Witch King... All gone.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You took them, didn't you?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I only needed to take the ones containing the clues.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: But I couldn't bear to part with the marigolds either.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...My suspicions were confirmed the moment you told me that you were there the night the Witch King died.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: When you cleaned the canvas back then, you left a spot untouched. The part showing you.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The Witch King's remnants were after witnesses to the Witch King's death.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And you were one of them.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But you're different from the others. You're not an innocent victim.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I... didn't want to say it. I didn't even want to ask.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why... couldn't I be selfish, just this once?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I really am sorry, Viviana.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why do I have to lose something I only just found?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: We should fight together, Concertmaster.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: The Gesatzswächter are here. We've come so far. It would be a shame to die at their hands now.

a.text: The amphitheater is a scene of chaos.
The tuning continues. The Ludwigs-Universität incident already proved that only the Kaiserinnen could fight Herkunftshorn's Arts.
What would the Twins think of my little show of selfishness, of betrayal?
I am not especially concerned.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: ...Do you believe that the Güldenesgesatz can completely change its tone?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I only care about the result.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The last person to rewrite the Güldenesgesatz was Herkunftshorn.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: But even he did not consider its destruction.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: The Movement is the foundation on which Leithanien is built.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Its destruction will undermine everything. Our aesthetics, our habits and usage of Arts, the Kurfürsten system, the imperial authority...

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: It will bring unprecedented change to Leithanien.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: But change isn't necessarily bad. If it were, we would never have been born.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: A pair of children born of Arts, in defiance of the laws of nature.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: 'This is just the beginning.'

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: That's what Fremont said to Leopold. We were but infants at the time, but I know you understood what they said as well as I did.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: We were born with a duty.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: A duty to change Leithanien.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Leopold was afraid of us. Which is why he had an army ready to tear us apart from behind the moment we killed Herkunftshorn.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: But we survived.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: ...We may not have chosen to be born, but once we were, we had the right to live.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Twenty-three years ago, we stood here gazing at the same sunset, over an altogether different scene of chaos.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You extended your hand to me before we began our long-awaited duet.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You said...

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: This sunset doesn't belong to anyone.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Not to Herkunftshorn, not to Leopold, not to the Kurfürsten, nor to any other ambitious noble.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Ja.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You took my hand, and we walked here together.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: There's no need to answer to the Kurfürsten... No need to be manipulated by anyone.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Our fate is ours alone to decide.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: And apparently... someone else shares the same desire.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Such a curious thing, the human soul.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: To think that even artificial children would learn human desire after gaining souls.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: That through a wish as simple as can be, the meek may be able to accomplish what even Herkunftshorn failed to, and redefine Leithanien.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: You want to ask whether I let Cora roam free on purpose, don't you?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Are you not of the same mind on this matter? Our thoughts are linked, even if it's been a long time since the two of us have watched the sunset together.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Let's stay a while. It won't take long.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: ...Very well.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: What will the future look like?

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Would you still watch it with me, Hildegard?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Where's Cora?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Viviana?

a.text: I could hear Brandt's voice. He's fighting the remaining cultists. They won't last long.
But the other is even faster.
Viviana is silent, but her Arts draw closer. I feel a shadow creep over the top of my foot, as cold as a storm at night.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Look out, Concertmaster!

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Concertmaster—

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: How... my Arts... went through...

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: This is... tuning? Why...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'm sorry, Amelie. Like I said, my decision has never changed.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Ha... haha... it's nothing. We've betrayed so many in our lifetimes... perhaps too many.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Herkunftshorn's eternal spire... It's so close... I'll be waiting for you... on the stairs...

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: ...Concertmaster.
Amelie must have turned to dark dust before me. This is how it is for the Witch King's followers. They don't want their bodies to linger on a land that lacks Herkunftshorn's favor.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: She's dead.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Most of them are. The remaining resistance will not last long.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: ...And the same for me, I suppose.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You deceived the followers of Herkunftshorn.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Ja. The Kaiserin's instruction was to become the Concertmaster of the Witch King's followers. To become a hope and a lure, and to lead them into the abyss by their own volition.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It's been twenty-three years. Everything about the Witch King—the long nightmares, the deep-rooted fears, the meaningless ambition—should have been gone from this country a long time ago.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So why is the 'tuning' still going?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Because...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Werner.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Did the Kaiserin order father's death?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: ...I tried to persuade him. I tried so hard.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I wanted him to hand over the copy of Güldenesgesatz, so I could move it elsewhere, but he was concerned that the Witch King remnants would catch on, thus nullifying the bait.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I asked him if maybe Brandt could arrive at the scene earlier, and save him at the scene of the attack... but he refused.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: He said he was already dying, and would soon get to see Lucinda. A few more days wasn't worth dragging both you and Sturmland into it.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: But you'd have gotten there if only he'd held out for a few more hours... or less.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: He was too determined to leave, and gave up too easily.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The day Werner died, I recovered the copy of the Movement and watched you return to Sturmland, walking the path paved for you, so similar to his...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: And I made the choice that had long been brewing in my heart.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...The Güldenesgesatz.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You're using Herkunftshorn's Arts to tune the music. You're trying to destroy it, or rather the influence it holds over all Leithanians.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: They say that fate is an endless spiral staircase.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: If so, the Güldenesgesatz is the staircase trapping Leithanien.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Stairs built a thousand years ago, glorious and beautiful on the outside, yet rotted to the core on the inside.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I've seen so many people trapped within. Herr Emmanuel, Gerhard, Frieda, Loris... and Brandt. All suffering the tidings of fate, helpless to change it.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The Witch King's Spire fell. Yet more rose to take its place. Those beneath the spires wish to climb them, while those atop them aspire to an even higher perch.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: They come and go, up and down, an endless waltz of hatred and conflict. Pain, sorrow and regret, filling the souls of one generation of Leithanians after another.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You too, Viviana. Once you enter the Kaiserinnen's Spires, you will only speak what they want you to.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I can 'see'... I have already seen how you will be forced to live a life you don't want, just like your father before you.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The Güldenesgesatz never changes. Leithanien never changes. Tragedy never changes.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Unless we free ourselves from the Movement of the past.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You say you want to change our fate. But who are you to decide who gets saved, and who gets sacrificed?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I can't. It's not my place, nor is it anyone's.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You want to destroy the old order. But where is the new order? Can you guarantee it will be better than yesterday or today?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I can't. Our future isn't for someone like me to decide.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Those who died for the plan, and the people right before us... don't you realize the pain they're in?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I hear them. Their screams, their laments... I will never stop hearing them, not until the day I die.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Then why do you have to be the one to change everything?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Because... I can.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: That's the only reason?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Someone has to. My life never had much meaning to begin with, except for one speck of light that never fully belonged to me. And I would do anything to keep it from going out.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I can't condone your cruelty, arrogance, or irresponsibility.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And as such, I must stop you.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Disaster has already struck, and by my hand. I've caused so much death, with even more to come.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Just stop this.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I can't. Not after what it took to get this far.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Do you know what it is about your actions I agree with the least?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You really are...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Heartless.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: No—!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Viviana...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Cora, Cora!

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I know, I know.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You're soft on the outside, but firm on the inside. You just can't turn your back on other people's pain.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You don't want to make things difficult for Brandt either. You're always thinking of others, even now.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: And... I'm glad I got to die at the hands of the one I love the most.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Are the clouds beautiful today?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: No need to be afraid, Viviana.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It'll pass. This will all...
She embraces me.
I can feel her hand on my back, trembling.
I want to hug her and comfort her like I used to. Perhaps I did. I talked so much, even though I had already begun to go numb from blood loss.
I can imagine her lake-like eyes beginning to rain, her gentle complexion warped by torment.
She only just learned that I've never clearly seen the faces of her father and mother.
Through Werner's words, I could only imagine how they looked, how they met, and how they fell in love.
After all, I went into that dark spire the day I came to Vedunien. And the day I left it, I could no longer see.
Everything I know that's nice and beautiful, including Brandt, was brought to me by Werner and Lucinda.
Except for one thing... except this.
The day that Werner brought the girl down from the spire to me, the day that I touched her soft, timid hand, the day that I wiped away her tears...
That was the day that I became certain of it.
I loved this child, and not because she was their daughter.
But because I saw in her something that none of us had.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You deserve a better life than this, Viviana... If there really is one...

a.text: Twenty-three years ago, I heard the sound of fighting from below, and gave the resonance pipeline at the top of the Spire a little push.
Just a little push, something anyone could do.
It created the tiniest gap in Herkunftshorn's defensive Arts. He had never imagined that a humble maidservant would have the courage to betray him.
Today, I tampered with the resonance pipelines of the Twin Empresses' Spires.
All I did was restore the Witch King's tuning components, according to the Arts he left behind in the copy of the Güldenesgesatz, then activate them with my own humble Arts.
Life is too short.
Do nothing, and you leave no trace behind, like the clouds floating past the spires.
But no one should drift with the wind like that, unable to determine their own future.
Many desires change. I'm just the first to extend my hand.
I hope that after this, all good people, all the people I love...
Will have a true future.
